trial_title: Evaluation of the Acceptability and Efficacy of 10 Micrograms of Estradiol Vaginal Tablets vs Promestriene Vaginal Cream
brief_summary: Evaluation of the Acceptability and Efficacy of 10 Micrograms of Estradiol Vaginal Tablets vs Promestriene Vaginal Cream in postmenopausal women aged 45 years or older, with one or more moderate to severe symptoms of vulvovaginal atrophy (dryness, dyspareunia, soreness or irritation).

eligibility_table.criterion: Postmenopausal women aged 45 years or older. Women will be considered postmenopausal with more than 12 months since last menstrual period
Women who have read and signed the Informed Consent Form
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's profile does not specify whether she has read and signed the Informed Consent Form.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient read and signed the Informed Consent Form for the trial?

eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a thin endometrium and no gestational sac, which may indicate an issue with uterine integrity.

eligibility_table.criterion: One or more vaginal symptoms (dryness, soreness, irritation, dyspareunia) rated as moderate to severe. Symptoms are moderate if the patient needs a treatment and feels discomfort. Symptoms are severe if the patient needs a treatment, and feels such a degree of discomfort that this could severely impact the subject's daily activities.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has vaginal spotting, but the severity of symptoms is not clearly rated as moderate to severe.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient report experiencing one or more vaginal symptoms (dryness, soreness, irritation, dyspareunia) rated as moderate to severe on a standardized symptom scale?
